questions.question: A bar is cut into 3 equal parts. What do we call each part?
questions.explain: When a whole is cut into 3 equal parts, each part is called a third. The name comes from how many equal parts there are, not from how many cuts you made.

questions.question: A bar is cut into 2 equal parts. What do we call each part?
questions.explain: A whole cut into 2 equal parts gives you halves. The number of equal parts tells the name, not the number of cuts.

questions.question: A bar is cut into 4 equal parts. What do we call each part?
questions.explain: 4 equal parts means each part is a fourth. Even though it takes 3 cuts, the parts are named by how many equal pieces there are.

questions.question: A bar is cut into 2 parts, but one part is much bigger than the other. Are they halves?
options: No, each part is a third
questions.explain: For parts to be halves, they must be the same size. If one piece is bigger, the parts are not equal, so they are not halves.

questions.question: Maya cuts a pizza into 3 equal slices. What is each slice called?
questions.explain: A pizza cut into 3 equal slices means each slice is one third. The name tells you how many equal parts the whole was cut into.

questions.question: A ribbon is cut into 4 pieces. Two pieces are long and two are short. How many fourths do you have?
questions.explain: For pieces to be called fourths, they must all be the same size. Since the pieces are different sizes, none of them are fourths.

questions.question: A bar is cut into 3 equal parts. A child points to one part and says, 'That is a half.' What should the child say?
questions.explain: The bar has 3 equal parts, so each part is a third. A half would mean the whole was cut into only 2 equal parts.

visual.caption: A bar split into 3 equal sections, 1 shaded

questions.question: Bar A is cut into 3 equal parts. Bar B is cut into 3 parts, but one part is smaller. Which bar shows thirds?
questions.explain: Thirds need 3 equal parts. Bar A has them, but Bar B does not because one piece is smaller. Only equal parts count as fraction parts.

questions.question: Nora wants to cut her banana bread into thirds for three friends. How should she cut it?
questions.explain: Thirds means 3 pieces that are all the same size. Cuts do not name the parts — 3 cuts across a loaf leave 4 pieces.

questions.question: Nadia folded her paper strip into equal parts. She coloured one part. Which sentence is true?
questions.explain: Count the equal parts: the strip has 3, so each one is a third. Folds are not parts — 2 folds across a strip leave 3 parts.

questions.question: Four friends want equal shares of one flatbread. Jamal cuts it into 4 pieces, but two pieces are much bigger. What is true?
questions.explain: Fourths are 4 parts that are all the same size. These pieces are different sizes, so no piece is a fourth.

questions.question: Mr. Chan cuts a pie for 2 children. Each child should get a half. What must he check?
questions.explain: Halves are 2 parts of the same size, so he compares the two pieces. Two pieces are not halves when one is bigger.

questions.question: Ella folds her paper strip in half. She folds it in half again. She opens the strip flat. What are the parts called?
questions.explain: Folding in half twice makes 4 parts that are all the same size, so they are fourths. Folds and creases do not name the parts.

questions.question: Dad cut this pie with 2 straight cuts. Every slice is the same size. What is the shaded slice called?
questions.explain: Count the equal slices, not the cuts. Two cuts across a pie make 4 equal slices, so one slice is a fourth.

questions.question: Mia's ribbon is 12 cm long. She cuts it into 3 pieces: 5 cm, 4 cm and 3 cm. Are the pieces thirds?
questions.explain: Thirds are 3 parts of the very same size. Real thirds of a 12 cm ribbon would each be 4 cm long.

questions.question: Ben cuts a sandwich into 4 equal pieces. He says each piece is a third because he made 3 cuts. What went wrong?
options: He named it by his parts
He made one cut too many
He named it by his cuts
questions.explain: Name the parts by counting the equal parts, not the cuts. The sandwich has 4 equal parts, so each piece is a fourth.
